genitive.basic_syntactic_functionality: The genitive qualifies, restricts, or describes the word it modifies, most often answering what kind.

genitive/adverbial.basic_syntactic_functionality: The genitive modifies the verbal idea rather than a substantive.

genitive/verbal.basic_syntactic_functionality: The genitive relates to a head noun that carries a verbal idea, standing as its subject or its object.

dative.basic_syntactic_functionality: The dative marks personal interest, location, or the means by which something occurs.

dative/adverbial.basic_syntactic_functionality: The dative modifies the verbal idea, supplying means, manner, or circumstance.

participle.basic_syntactic_functionality: A verbal adjective, carrying both the tense and voice of a verb and the case, gender, and number of an adjective.

participle/adjectival.basic_syntactic_functionality: The participle ascribes an action or quality directly to a substantive.

participle/adverbial.basic_syntactic_functionality: The participle modifies the main verb, supplying the circumstance under which its action occurs.

genitive/adverbial/time.description: The genitive substantive indicates the kind of time within which the verbal action occurs, answering 'during what sort of time'.
soft_constraints: Contrast the accusative, which stresses extent of time, and the dative, which stresses a point in time.

reference_card.sentence: νυκτὸς ὁ ἄνθρωπος γράφει τὸν λόγον.
reference_card.translation: During the night the man writes the word.

genitive/verbal/subjective.description: The genitive substantive functions as the subject of the verbal idea implicit in the head noun.
hard_constraints: The head noun must carry a verbal idea, one with a cognate verb.
soft_constraints: Where the head noun's verb is transitive, the objective genitive is the nearest competing reading.

dative/adverbial/means.description: The dative substantive names the impersonal means or instrument by which the verbal action is accomplished.
hard_constraints: The dative substantive must be impersonal.
A personal agent requires ὑπό with the genitive, not a bare dative.
soft_constraints: The dative of manner is the nearest competing reading where the substantive is abstract.

reference_card.sentence: ὁ θεὸς λύει τὸν ἄνθρωπον τῷ λόγῳ.
reference_card.translation: God releases the man by the word.

participle/adjectival/attributive.description: The participle functions as an adjective, ascribing a quality or action directly to the substantive it modifies.
hard_constraints: The participle must agree with its substantive in gender, number, and case.
When articular, the participle must stand in an attributive position.
soft_constraints: The substantival participle is the nearest competing reading where no head noun is expressed.

reference_card.sentence: ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ λέγων τὸν λόγον πιστεύει.
reference_card.translation: The man who speaks the word believes.

participle/adverbial/genitive_absolute.description: A participial clause, grammatically detached from the main clause, in which a genitive noun or pronoun serves as the subject of a genitive participle.
hard_constraints: Both the participle and its subject must be genitive.
The subject of the participle must not be the subject of the main verb.
soft_constraints: It most often stands at the head of the sentence and carries temporal force.

reference_card.sentence: λέγοντος τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ὁ θεὸς γράφει.
reference_card.translation: While the man is speaking, God writes.
